title: Ops dependency deconflict cadence and comms guide
content:
Purpose
- Quick reference and working plan to run a lightweight, repeatable 'deconflict cadence' across product, infra, serving-runtime, and platform teams to unblock SLO changes, capacity requests, and fallback policy rollouts.
- Goal: reduce last-minute rollbacks and mismatched expectations by catching cross-team constraints 7-14 days before a risky change.

Scope
- Applies to: any SLO change, capacity/freq policy change, model variant fallback, routing policy update, or infra maintenance that can affect p50/p95 latency or error-rate signals for customer-facing routes.
- Excludes: pure docs edits, non-production config tweaks that don't touch traffic routing.

Stakeholders / Roles (lean)
- Change Owner (product/feature team): responsible for proposal + runbook.
- Dependency Liaisons (one per team): eng-sre, serving-runtime, infra, platform, console. They surface constraints and sign off on mitigations.
- Release Gatekeeper (SRE lead): coordinates final go/no-go window with oncall.
- Observability Sponsor: owns alerting and dashboard updates for the change.

Cadence (lightweight weekly + async)
1) T-14 days: Proposal posted to shared "deconflict board" (Confluence + annotated Jira) with expected risk, affected SLOs, traffic % change, rollout plan, and rollback plan.
2) Within 48h: Dependency liaisons add blockers or OKs on the board. If any liaison marks "needs action", owner must schedule a short sync.
3) T-7 days: Intake review (15m async sync via Slack thread + triage note). If unresolved items remain, schedule 30m cross-team sync.
4) T-3 days: Final readiness check. Release Gatekeeper publishes go/no-go checklist.
5) Post-release (T+1 day and T+7 days): owner posts short postmortem + SLO signal check.

Communication channels and artifacts
- Primary async: #reliability-deconflict Slack channel (thread-per-change). Use message template: /deconflict: <JIRA> <TL;DR> <SLO impact> <owner> <T-date>.
- Confluence board: canonical dependency table with columns: change-id, owner, affected-SLOs, liaison-ok, blockers, mitigation, estimated-impact, rollback-window.
- Jira linkage: always link to a Jira ticket (label: slo-deconflict).
- Weekly digest: short email pulse to stakeholders summarizing upcoming high-risk changes.

Decision rubric (how liaisons should evaluate changes)
- Low concern: p95 change <10ms, error delta <0.05% on small subset (<1% traffic), rollout <5%. OK to auto-approve.
- Medium concern: p95 change 10-50ms or error delta 0.05-0.5% or rollout 5-25% OR involves routing fallback. Require remediation note + liaison acknowledgement.
- High concern: p95 >50ms or error delta >0.5% OR affects multiple regions/customers or stateful infra change. Requires cross-team sync and explicit Release Gatekeeper approval.

Quick templates (copy into Slack/Confluence/Jira)
- Slack /deconflict template: <JIRA> | owner: <name> | when: <T-date> | risk: low/medium/high | SLOs: p50/p95/err | notes: <one-line>
- Confluence dependency row example: change-id: SRE-3423 | owner: Maya Chen | SLOs: gen-api p95 | liaison-ok: serving-runtime: yes | blockers: infra disk maintenance windows | mitigation: shift canary to region-b | rollback window: 30m

Meeting agenda (30m cross-team sync)
- 0-5m: owner TL;DR + what success looks like.
- 5-12m: liaison reports (infra, runtime, observability).
- 12-20m: open blockers + mitigation assignment.
- 20-28m: clear go/no-go criteria and rollback triggers.
- 28-30m: action items and owners.

Escalation flow and timers
- If a liaison raises 'blocking' less than T-3 days, Release Gatekeeper must be notified immediately and a decision made within 6 hours.
- On-call may pause any rollout for immediate investigation; pause requires a short blameless message in Slack and update to Confluence board.

Lightweight artifacts to create per change
- One-line TL;DR in Slack + link to Jira.
- Runbook page (Confluence) with metrics to watch, dashboard links, and rollback steps.
- Short checklist file attached to Jira (go/no-go boolean fields).

Operational metrics (what we track to measure effectiveness)
- % of changes with liaison OKs before T-7. Target: 90%
- Median days between proposal and first approval. Target: >=7 days
- Number of rollbacks triggered by cross-team misses. Target: reduce by 50% vs prior quarter
- Time to mitigation after liaison flags a blocker (target <24h for medium, <6h for high)

Risks and mitigations (notes to self)
- Risk: slack-thread fatigue -> mitigation: weekly digest + move low-risk to auto-approve flow.
- Risk: too much overhead for small teams -> mitigation: narrow scope to SLO-impacting changes only and provide templated runbooks.
- Risk: teams ignore cadence -> mitigation: escalate to managers and surface missed signoffs in quarterly reliability review.

Open questions / To decide
- Should we require liaison signoff in Jira (yes/no)? (pros: auditable; cons: extra friction)
- Do we lock a maintenance window calendar for regional infra operations that blocks rollouts?
- How to measure 'customer-impacting' more concretely for multi-tenant routes?

Next steps (owner: Maya)
- Draft Confluence board skeleton and link to this doc (by 2026-11-05).
- Seed Slack channel with two upcoming changes and test the /deconflict template (by 2026-11-09).
- Run a 30m trial cadence with platform + serving-runtime the week of 2026-11-15 and capture feedback.

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally lightweight and opinionated. Please add blockers as comments on the Confluence skeleton (linked artifact above) rather than editing this doc.
- If you think the decision rubric thresholds should be different for embeddings vs generative APIs, call it out in your review.
